title: Your Digital Footprint
objective: Learn OSINT basics by investigating your OWN digital footprint, understand Google dorking for self-discovery, manage privacy settings, practice OPSEC, and learn how photo metadata can reveal your location.
explanation:
Every time you post on social media, sign up for a website, comment on a video, or even just browse the internet, you leave digital traces. This collection of traces is called your digital footprint, and it might reveal far more about you than you realize.

OSINT (Open Source Intelligence) is the practice of gathering information from publicly available sources — search engines, social media, public records, websites, and metadata. Professional OSINT analysts use these techniques to investigate criminals, track threats, and verify identities. But here's the catch: everything they can find about a target, someone can find about YOU.

In this lesson, you'll use OSINT techniques exclusively on YOURSELF. You'll Google your own name, check what data breaches your email has been in, examine photo metadata, and learn what you're accidentally sharing. The goal isn't to stalk others — it's to understand your own exposure and lock it down.

Google dorking means using advanced search operators to find specific information. For example, 'site:instagram.com "your name"' shows what Instagram pages mention you. 'filetype:pdf "your name"' finds PDFs containing your name. These are powerful tools — and anyone can use them to find information about you.

OPSEC (Operational Security) is the practice of protecting sensitive information by viewing your activities from an adversary's perspective. Ask yourself: What could someone learn about me from my public profiles? Could they figure out where I live, work, or go to school? Could they use this info for social engineering?

Photo metadata (EXIF data) is particularly sneaky. When your phone takes a picture, it silently records the GPS coordinates, camera model, date, time, and sometimes your device's serial number. If you post that photo without stripping the metadata, anyone can find out exactly where you were standing. In this lesson, you'll check YOUR OWN photos for metadata and learn how to remove it.

Remember: ALL OSINT in this lesson is on YOURSELF. Investigating other people without their consent raises serious ethical and legal concerns.

commands.command:
python3 -c "
print('=== GOOGLE DORK CHEAT SHEET (For Searching YOURSELF Only) ===')
print()
dorks = [
    ('site:instagram.com \"your name\"', 'Find mentions of your name on Instagram'),
    ('site:linkedin.com \"your name\"', 'Find your LinkedIn profile and any public posts'),
    ('site:facebook.com \"your name\"', 'Find your Facebook profile and tagged posts'),
    ('\"your.email@gmail.com\"', 'Find where your email address appears publicly'),
    ('\"your name\" filetype:pdf', 'Find PDFs containing your name (school docs, etc.)'),
    ('\"your name\" site:reddit.com', 'Find Reddit posts mentioning your name'),
    ('intitle:\"your username\"', 'Find pages with your username in the title'),
    ('\"your phone number\"', 'Check if your phone number appears online'),
]
for dork, desc in dorks:
    print(f'  {dork}')
    print(f'    -> {desc}')
    print()
print('IMPORTANT: Replace \"your name\" with YOUR actual name.')
print('ONLY search for YOUR OWN information. Never use these to investigate others.')
"
commands.description: Displays Google dorking operators you can use to search for YOUR OWN information across the internet. Replace the placeholders with your actual name, email, and username to see what's publicly visible about you.
commands.expectedOutput:
=== GOOGLE DORK CHEAT SHEET (For Searching YOURSELF Only) ===
  site:instagram.com "your name"
    -> Find mentions of your name on Instagram
...
IMPORTANT: Replace "your name" with YOUR actual name.
ONLY search for YOUR OWN information.
commands.troubleshooting: Remember to put your name in quotes for exact match. Without quotes, Google searches for each word separately. Use a private/incognito browser window so your own browsing history doesn't affect results.

commands.command:
python3 -c "
print('=== METADATA REMOVAL COMMANDS ===')
print()
commands = [
    ('exiftool -all= photo.jpg', 'Strip ALL metadata from a photo'),
    ('exiftool -gps:all= photo.jpg', 'Strip only GPS data, keep other metadata'),
    ('mat2 document.pdf', 'Remove metadata from PDFs (install: sudo apt install mat2)'),
    ('mat2 --show document.pdf', 'Show what metadata exists in a file'),
    ('exiftool -r -all= ./photos/', 'Recursively strip metadata from all photos in a folder'),
]
for cmd, desc in commands:
    print(f'  {cmd}')
    print(f'    -> {desc}')
    print()
print('ALWAYS strip metadata before sharing photos or documents online.')
print('Many social media platforms strip EXIF data automatically (Instagram, Twitter),')
print('but others (like email, forums, cloud storage) may preserve it.')
"
commands.description: Provides a reference sheet of commands for removing metadata from photos and documents. These are essential tools for maintaining privacy when sharing files online.
commands.expectedOutput:
=== METADATA REMOVAL COMMANDS ===
  exiftool -all= photo.jpg
    -> Strip ALL metadata from a photo
...
ALWAYS strip metadata before sharing photos or documents online.
commands.troubleshooting: If exiftool is not installed: 'sudo apt install libimage-exiftool-perl'. For mat2: 'sudo apt install mat2'. Both are available in Kali's default repositories.

challenge.question: You want to check your digital footprint. You Google 'site:reddit.com "hackeryoung"' and find a Reddit post from 2 years ago where you mentioned your school name and the city you live in. What steps should you take?
challenge.hint: Think about what information is now exposed and what an attacker could do with your school + city + username combination. Then think about both removing the data and preventing future leaks.
challenge.answer: Steps to take: (1) Delete the Reddit post immediately if possible. If you can't (e.g., deleted your account), contact Reddit to request removal. (2) Check if the 'hackeryoung' username is used on other platforms — an attacker could link your Reddit post to your other accounts and combine information. (3) If the same username is used elsewhere, consider changing it on platforms where you share personal info. (4) Google your school name + city + 'hackeryoung' to see if the combination reveals more about you. (5) Going forward, never share identifying details (school, city, age, neighborhood) on accounts linked to your usual username. (6) Consider using separate usernames for different contexts — one for gaming, one for tech forums, etc.

realWorld: In 2021, a cyberstalker used OSINT techniques to track down a streamer's physical location using only background details visible in their live streams — reflections in windows, landmarks visible through curtains, and delivery box labels that briefly appeared on camera. The stalker showed up at their apartment. This case highlights why understanding your digital footprint isn't just about data privacy — it's about physical safety. The streamer now uses a P.O. box, blurs backgrounds, and strips metadata from all shared content.
funFact: Journalist John McAfee (creator of McAfee antivirus) was hiding from authorities in Guatemala in 2012. A reporter from VICE magazine posted a photo with him — without stripping the EXIF metadata. The GPS coordinates in the photo revealed McAfee's exact hiding location, and he was found by police shortly after. One photo's metadata ended a weeks-long international manhunt.
